items.title: Mozambique’s exchange rate reform aims for gradual shift towards a market-led exchange rate – minister
items.summary: “We also have the chapter on exchange rate reform, which aims to move gradually and in a guided manner towards a market-led exchange rate,” Carla Loveira said, presenting measures under way or planned at a meeting with businesspeople in Maputo The position, expressed during a meeting held as part of a Business Breakfast dedicated to fiscal policy, the business environment and private-sector priorities for the country’s economic growth, organised by the Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA), comes amid debate over difficulties in accessing foreign currency and the process by which the central bank sets the exchange rate In practice, due to the lack of access to foreign currency through the banking system, businesspeople end up resorting to buying currency through alternative channels, at rates considerably above the official exchange rate.

items.title: Ethiopian PM puts ministers through military training
items.summary: The training comes as Ethiopia faces continued fighting in parts of the northern Tigray region Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has put his cabinet ministers and other senior government officials through military training, saying armed forces discipline can help build stronger leaders and advance the country's development Photos shared by him on social media show him taking part in military exercises alongside ministers, deputy ministers and heads of government institutions at the Hurso military training centre The move is unusual in Ethiopia, where senior civilian government officials are rarely seen undergoing military training Those taking part include Speaker of the House of Federation Muferiat Kamil, Finance Minister Fitsum Assefa and Health Minister Mekdes Daba It is unclear when the training began or how long it is expected to last In his post, the prime minister, who is known as Abiy, said Ethiopia's ambition to achieve universal prosperity required its leadership to be physically fit, morally strong and intellectually capable He said military institutions offered…

items.title: INE records over 14,000 registered non-profit entities in Mozambique
items.summary: Maputo, 30 Oct (AIM) – Mozambique’s National Statistics Institute (INE) has recorded 14,462 formally registered non-profit entities, as part of the 3rd Business Census (CEMPRE 2025-2026). According to the census – which was conducted between September 2025 and May 2026, aiming to collect and update information on the structure of the Mozambican business sector, non-profit institutions – the country has 112,784 formally registered companies. The study points out that these non-profit institutions employ 136,269 people and generate approximately 117.4 billion meticais in annual revenue (1.8 billion US dollars at the current exchange rate). 50.7 percent of these institutions are associations, followed by religious organizations at 45.5 percent. The southern provinces Inhambane and of Gaza, and the central province of Manica, account together 67.4 percent of the country’s non-profit institutions. On the other hand, INE recorded the formal existence of 112.784 companies in the country, which corresponds to 80.1 percent.

items.title: Spain train disaster clouds Sánchez chances of re-election
items.summary: The breaking news from Spain this week was shocking but also shockingly familiar: another collision on the high-speed rail line south from Madrid, with reports of dozens killed It is just nine months since two trains crashed near Cordoba, killing 46 people. Now 69 bodies have been recovered here in central Spain, from wreckage strewn over the tracks and down an embankment For the victims' families it is devastating; a personal tragedy But it is also a national disaster that has shattered confidence in the country's rail network and the Socialist-led government of Pedro Sánchez.
